subject: Derivatives suppression, evidence pack & SLA exception — kickoff
messages:
From: Olivia King <olivia.king@novumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Derivative suppression + DPA questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick call yesterday. As we start procurement for the Novum pilot, legal has a couple of non-negotiables around LLM data use that I want to capture in writing so procurement can move the contract forward:

- Explicit commitment that Novum customer interactions will not be used to improve or retrain Redwood models (no model improvement) for hosted and dedicated options.
- Confirmation Novum retains ownership of prompts and generated responses; Redwood will not assert derivative IP rights.
- A reproducible evidence path we can hand to auditors: proof-of-deletion for logs, a subprocessor inventory, and a way to export tenant interactions (SFTP or similar) on request.
- A note on export formats and whether interactive-session transcripts and ephemeral KV are included.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a contractual clause + operational playbook for the above? If yes, procurement needs the DPA redline and an operations runbook by end of next week (target: 2026-11-19).

Appreciate it — cc'ing Marco (security) for any technical clarifications.

Thanks,
Olivia King
Head of Procurement, Novum Health
olivia.king@novumhealth.com

--

From: Olivia King <olivia.king@novumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Silva <marco.silva@novumhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Derivative suppression + DPA questions

Thanks Marissa — a couple of clarifications before you draft clauses: 

1) For Hosted API: we understand restrictions are possible at the tenant/config level. Procurement needs a written guarantee that Novum data will be excluded from any model improvement pipelines—explicitly called out in the DPA (no ambiguous "use" language).

2) Proof-of-deletion: auditors require a signed attestation plus a machine-verifiable artifact showing deletion timestamps and the unique keys of deleted archives. Will Redwood provide a cryptographic deletion log or similar?

3) Export scope: we need transcripts of interactive sessions, request/response payloads, and the user-supplied prompt text. Ephemeral KV should be documented when it is persisted vs ephemeral.

4) Subprocessors: we expect a current list and a simple gating process for adding new subprocessors (30-day notice at minimum).

5) SLA exception: security wants logs retained for 90 days for debugging during pilot. Is Redwood willing to grant a temporary exception from standard retention rules with an operational control to limit access?

If you can cover these items in the package, we can move to legal review and sign.

Olivia

--

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Derivative suppression + DPA questions — proposed language

Hi Olivia — thanks for the detailed asks. Attached below is the contract excerpt we propose for the DPA (inline for speed). If you want redlines back in a PDF I can send the redline DPA as well.

Proposed DPA excerpt (for discussion):
"Customer Data; No-Model-Improvement. Customer Data means any content, inputs, prompts, outputs, metadata and logs that Customer submits to the Service. Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve, train, fine-tune or otherwise modify machine learning models \"for any purpose\" without Customer's prior written consent. For Hosted offerings, Redwood will provide an exclusion configuration for Customer such that Customer Data is excluded from model-training pipelines.

Proof of Deletion. Upon Customer request Redwood will provide an attestation of deletion and an export of deletion receipts containing object identifiers and deletion timestamps for the Customer Data. Deletion receipts are retained for 180 days to support audit requests.

Ownership. Customer retains all intellectual property rights in Customer prompts and outputs; Redwood disclaims any ownership in Customer-provided prompts and Customer-generated outputs.

Subprocessors. Redwood will provide a current subprocessor inventory and will provide 30 days' notice prior to onboarding any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data; Customer may reasonably object in writing.

We can add a temporary SLA carveout in a Schedule A that permits retention of access logs for up to 90 days for pilot debugging; access will be limited to named Redwood engineers and logged.

Questions for Novum: preferred export mechanism (SFTP vs S3 presigned link) and whether you require onshore-only key management (KMS) for exported artifacts.

If that language looks OK I’ll prepare a marked DPA and send for signature.

—Ben
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Derivative suppression + DPA questions — ops playbook and inventory

Hi Olivia / Marco — following up with operational details and the attachments referenced below. Summary of what we will deliver in the package by 2026-11-19: 

1) Ops export playbook (attached: ops-export-playbook-20261116.md) — includes SFTP and AS2 export options, schema for exports (JSONL with session_id, timestamp, request_payload, response_payload, prompt_meta), and an operator checklist for redaction.
2) Subprocessor inventory (attached CSV) — current list with country, function, and data residency.
3) Deletion evidence: we provide deletion receipts that include object_id, deletion_timestamp (ISO8601), and deletion_hash (SHA256). Deletion receipts are signed with Redwood's system key and stored for 180 days. If Novum requires a cryptographic proof-of-deletion notarized external to Redwood, we can discuss an escrow approach (additional fees apply).
4) SLA carveout: for the pilot we will permit a 90-day debug-log retention window limited to a named access list; at the end of the pilot logs will be purged and receipts provided. This will be a Schedule in the DPA.

Attachments included with this email: redwood-dpa-draft-NovumHealth-v1.2.pdf; subprocessor-inventory-20261110.csv; ops-export-playbook-20261116.md

Operational question — preferred export transport: please confirm SFTP endpoint and account contact or if you prefer a pre-signed S3 link into an EU-region account that you control. For onshore KMS, please confirm whether Novum requires EU-region KMS or a Novum-managed KMS key.

Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
